title: 250 Years of American Capitalism: Hamilton, the GFC, & the AI Boom | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 71
summary: Adrian Wooldridge surveys American capitalism from Hamilton through industrialization and financial crises. The main investment lesson is that transformative infrastructure need not reward its investors. Eisman independently challenges the book GFC account, emphasizing leverage rather than housing policy alone. Primary commission evidence supports that emphasis while limiting stronger claims about a single regulatory cause and a panic-free counterfactual. Long-run AI and institutional analogies remain unproven; the claimed Roosevelt inauguration timing is contradicted by a contemporaneous record.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Separate social value from returns on invested capital.
Examine leverage and funding mechanisms rather than only the initial asset shock.
Treat historical analogies as hypotheses requiring matched economic structure.
Distinguish reported coauthor views from guest beliefs.
tools_and_charts: Economies of scale and unit costs
transcript_cautions: Captions say trans-Pacific for transcontinental and Clark for the 1873 bank reference.
Greenspan historical views are often secondhand and qualified.
Limited-liability discussion is clarified by the host; invested capital still remains at risk.
Ads are excluded from analyst claims.
